column12: Judgement: house convention. Balversa is the closest marketed comparator: the only approved FGFR inhibitor in urothelial cancer, and oral like vepugratinib. The case against is that it is used later-line as monotherapy, with a median PFS of 5.6 months in THOR (NEJM 2023, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2308849). A beneficiary's spend therefore covers well under a year of therapy, and this figure understates an annual price. Retail quotes of about $28,000 a month for 8 mg daily (drugs.com, GoodRx) would annualise to roughly $330,000, but that is not a named manufacturer list price, so the convention stands. A reviewer may also argue that a first-line add-on to an IV regimen would be priced below monotherapy. The two effects pull in opposite directions.

column12: Stated as a share of incidence. The 11,600 dates from a flow model built on an incidence near 81,000, so it is a slightly older base. The case for a lower figure: a nationwide registry finds FGFR3 in about 15% of metastatic cases, and Haas et al. (Eur Urol Open Sci 2025, PMID 40521274) find it in 16 of 113 metastatic tumours (14%); the 20% comes from a Foundation Medicine clinicogenomic cohort, which may over-represent patients sequenced for a reason. The FORAGER-2 abstract itself says 15-20%. The label pool includes upper-tract disease, which FORAGER-2 enrols and which the SEER bladder count excludes. Applied to the book's 763,031 prevalence this gives an opening stock of 20,942, which a first-line pool does not have. See untreated_carryover_pct

column12: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0. Vepugratinib is an add-on to EV+P, so its ceiling is the share of FGFR3-altered first-line patients who receive EV+P. The peak is set at EV+P's measured capture. The case for lower: incomplete FGFR3 testing before first-line therapy, added FGFR toxicity (hyperphosphataemia, ocular and nail events) on top of EV's neuropathy and rash, and the fact that a positive PFS result is not guaranteed to change practice. The case for higher: EV+P share was still rising after 2024, reaching 62% of first-line starts in 2025 in the same dataset
